clue.text: Running dogs I have to follow behind

indicators.note: the second piece is told to come after the first, trailing it

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone is told to trot along at the back after a pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like part of the dog scene but is the definition: cursive script is running handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursive handwriting has its letters joined in a flowing hand, also called a running hand.

clue.text: In which a steer is restrained

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words which a steer

explanation.surface: A description of a container in which a young bullock is held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained' looks like part of the cattle picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, holding back from excess.

clue.text: Bitterness in private hearing

indicators.note: a word heard spoken, so the answer sounds like the soldier's name

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: Resentment aired at a closed court session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private hearing' suggests a court sitting in camera, but 'private' is a ranker and 'hearing' signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment or ill feeling.

clue.text: "I will turn up", I state — it's unreasonable

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
taken as written
Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone vows to show up, then admits the promise makes no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical means lacking sound reasoning, so senseless.

clue.text: Soldiers turned up and sallied out in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue the corps' letters are written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: the letters of sallied are put out of order

explanation.surface: Troops arrived and made an excursion into the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses REME to EMER; 'out' rearranges SALLIED into ALDISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is poetically called after the vivid green of its landscape.

clue.text: A drinking man

explanation.surface: A man who drinks a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long swallow of liquid is a gulp or a drinking; one of the round pieces moved in the board game checkers is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Girl's portion

explanation.surface: A young woman's share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Dot is short for Dorothy; a dot (dowry) is an old word for a bride's marriage portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a pet form of the name Dorothy; it is also an archaic term for a dowry, the portion a bride brings.

clue.text: A stance taken up by author

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is lifted upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a pose is a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A writer adopts a particular position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses POSE to ESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek writer of fables.

clue.text: Primate installs running water in former Portuguese territory

indicators.note: the stream is set within the territory's name

parts.note: Goa was a Portuguese colony in India until 1961
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An ape fits plumbing in an old colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installs' joins the definition to the wordplay, and 'in' puts RILL inside GOA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gorilla is the largest of the great apes.

clue.text: Discuss one's English paper

parts.note: to treat a subject is to discuss it
one is I, so one's is I's

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk about someone's English essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work on a subject, as an academic paper is.

clue.text: Making void the marriage of girl to several fellows in the last month

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: the fellows sit inside the abbreviation for last month

parts.note: ult. (ultimo) means of last month in old business letters
men are fellows, plural

explanation.surface: A news item about a woman who married several men last month and had it all cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT, short for ultimo, is an old commercial abbreviation meaning 'of last month'.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment is a legal declaration that a wedding never validly existed.

clue.text: Worker leaves police officer worsted

indicators.note: the worker departs from the officer's title, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a sergeant is a rank of police officer
an ant is the classic crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: A worker walks out on a police officer who has been beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worsted' reads as 'defeated' but is the definition: worsted is a woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric of the worsted kind.

clue.text: Thin strip of material needs a press right away

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is sent off, so it is taken out of the crowd word

parts.note: a press of people is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A narrow piece of fabric must be ironed immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press right away' looks like 'iron at once'; 'press' is a crowd and 'right away' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow leather strap or lace, or a skimpy garment of narrow fabric.

clue.text: George is a car driver

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a pilot drives or steers a craft

explanation.surface: Someone named George works as a chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George.

clue.text: Army fast to reject one seeking potential for entertainment

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve
Lent is the Christian period of fasting
to scout an idea is to dismiss it scornfully

explanation.surface: Soldiers are quick to turn away someone looking for performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quick' but is Lent; 'scout' is an old verb meaning to scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person searches for gifted newcomers for show business or sport.

clue.text: A line of children hurries to produce a show of emotion

parts.note: in Britain a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs
tears means rushes along

explanation.surface: A file of rushing schoolchildren causes a display of feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is the British name for schoolchildren walking two by two in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping is named after the legend that the reptile weeps while eating its prey.

clue.text: Is patriot indisposed in a clipper?…

indicators.note: being out of sorts, the letters of these words are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A question whether a sick nationalist is aboard a fast sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipper' suggests a ship, but here it is one who clips hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: A topiarist shapes hedges and shrubs by cutting them, so a clipper of greenery.

clue.text: … I cross miserably in steamer or cutter

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the steamer's abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: used wretchedly, the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Continuing the clipper theme, someone is unhappily crossing in a steamship or a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' rearranges I CROSS to CISSOR, put 'in' SS. A cutter is also a boat, the false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are a cutting tool with two blades.

clue.text: Visions of saints in places that are extraordinary

indicators.note: being out of the ordinary, the letters of these words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Religious visions of holy figures appearing in remarkable places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are extraordinary' rearranges SAINTS IN PLACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydream schemes that can never be realised are idle fancies, so visions in the sense of fantasies.

clue.text: Weapon — it finally pierces warlord

indicators.note: the letter stabs into the warlord's title

parts.note: a shogun was a military ruler of Japan

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word it is used

explanation.surface: A weapon finally runs a military leader through.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm.

clue.text: What oilmen do, lacking society, in small reservoir

indicators.note: the abbreviation is missing, so it is taken out

parts.note: oilmen sink a well when drilling

explanation.surface: Drillers' activity minus social life, in a little reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small reservoir' looks like a place oilmen work but is the definition: a pot of ink on a desk.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell is a small container of ink set into a desk.

clue.text: Point, perhaps, and mock when someone good comes in

indicators.note: the good person enters the mocking word

parts.note: to jeer is to mock
St is the abbreviation for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A remark about mockery that stops when a virtuous person enters.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Point is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Yeomen of the Guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Point is a court fool in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera, an example of the type.

clue.text: The latest way to govern tyrannically

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to oppress is to rule cruelly

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the newest method of ruling as a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop press' was the late news added to a newspaper after printing began.
explanation.definitionFit: Late news inserted in a paper at the last minute was printed under this heading, so it is the newest news.

clue.text: Quiet girl in velvet

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A quiet girl dressed in velvet.
explanation.definitionFit: Panne is a lustrous velvet with a flattened pile.

clue.text: An animal seen around the joint _

indicators.note: the animal is turned round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: Some creature has been spotted hanging round a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' turns ELK into KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge where foot meets leg.

clue.text: … or an animal seen around the vehicle

indicators.note: the horse is turned round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Or some creature is seen hanging around the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' turns NAG into GAN. 'vehicle' is used in its sense of a medium or means of expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper that serves as the mouthpiece of a party is its organ, a means or medium of communication.

clue.text: Exercising foresight, supply books

parts.note: to provide is to supply
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Being far-sighted, someone stocks up on reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means thrifty and planning for the future.

clue.text: Bird food

explanation.surface: Something for a bird to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie is an old name for the magpie; it is also a baked dish with a pastry crust.

clue.text: Genuine increase, without a misrepresentation

indicators.note: the letters are falsely presented, so they are rearranged once the a is set aside

parts.note: taken as written, the letter removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A real rise, with no distortion of the figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A from INCREASE ('without a') and rearrange the remaining INCRESE ('misrepresentation').
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and heartfelt, so real rather than feigned.

clue.text: The holder of a duty-free office

definitions.text: The holder of a duty-free office

parts.words: The holder of a duty-free office
parts.note: not a shop at an airport but someone with a post that carries the name and no real functions

explanation.definitionFit: A titular holder bears a title in name only, without the work or authority that should go with it.
